summary: Remmel Mountain's 1930 ground cab in the Pasayten Wilderness served as a 1942 aircraft-warning post and was gone by 1952; no source describes what remains.

facts.design: Ground-mounted Region-5 cab; a 1950 survey described a 14-foot-square wooden building with a gable roof
facts.status_note: Cab gone since 1952; no source describes what remains on the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Okanogan National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot from trailheads in the Pasayten Wilderness. WillhiteWeb says the Andrews Creek route burned and was closed for many years.

visit.trail_note: About 16 miles one way from the Thirtymile, Cathedral Driveway or Andrews Creek trailheads; the WTA lists an abandoned side trail to the old lookout location

events.note: An International Boundary Commission party reported a trail and a lookout house on the summit; WillhiteWeb calls the first building unclear
Other survey parties reported a lookout building and trail
Ground-mounted Region-5 cab built per the register; a 1930 newspaper item says Ed Allen was building a new lookout station
Keith Patterson served as the summer lookout
Aircraft Warning Service station, activated July 8 and deactivated August 31, 1942
A 1950 survey party said the Forest Service had abandoned the lookout house for service due to safety factors
Inventory suggests 1952; WillhiteWeb and firelookout.com say destroyed, while the FFLOS register says removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and inventory date the cab to 1930, and a 1930 newspaper item reports a new station under construction. WillhiteWeb cites earlier reports of a lookout house in 1904 and a lookout building in 1925 and calls the first building unclear, so the 1930 cab may not have been the first structure.
A 1932 newspaper item gives 8,690 feet; the register gives 8,685 feet. The sources differ by five feet, and the story gives both.
The FFLOS register says removed in 1952; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1952. The year agrees, and only the verb differs.
WillhiteWeb calls the summit trail a nice trail; the WTA lists a side trail to the old lookout location as abandoned. They may describe different routes, so current conditions should be checked.

notes_for_editor: Build (1930) and removal (1952) agree across sources; only the verb differs (removed vs destroyed). The 1930 and 1932 newspaper items are read through Rex's Fire Lookout Page, a secondary transcription; the original Wenatchee Daily World was not checked. Elevation differs by 5 ft (8,685 register vs 8,690 in 1932 item). Trail and access notes are undated (WillhiteWeb, WTA); the Andrews Creek closure may be out of date. Nothing on the summit today is described by any source, so the story says so. Record coordinates match the FFLOS point; no corrections.
